title: the Marlowe Estate Rising Revisited
premise: Theo Halloran, archivist of St. Aldric's Cathedral, receives a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral of Sir Edmund Marlowe — a man Theo never met but whose family crypt sits locked beneath the cathedral for reasons erased from every record. Following the letter's clues, Theo discovers the Marlowe estate's 'rising' — a 1947 flood that supposedly drowned the original house — was staged to hide a murder and a stolen identity: Edmund's father never existed, and the man buried as him was a servant who took his place. As Theo decodes a ledger hidden in plain sight in the cathedral's own donation plaques, they realize the confession was written by Edmund's still-living sister, who killed her brother to keep the secret from surfacing before the statute of limitations expires. In the crypt's final reckoning, Theo must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile belonging they've finally found — and chooses truth, sealing the ledger into the public record and unlocking the crypt at last.
about_author: Jonah Montrose is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing documents no one asked to read. They write mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: Postmarked the Day After
chapters.summary: Theo Halloran, cathedral archivist, sorts the condolence mail for Sir Edmund Marlowe's funeral and finds a confession letter dated one day after the death. Its author is unnamed; its promise, 'the crypt will tell you the rest,' is impossible — the crypt has been sealed for seventy years. POV: Theo. Beat: uneasy curiosity masquerading as professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt of St. Aldric's
chapters.summary: Theo investigates the crypt's sealing, finding a 1947 order citing 'structural risk' signed by a Marlowe trustee — the same week the Marlowe estate house allegedly drowned in a flood. The dean warns Theo off. POV: Theo. Beat: first friction between duty and the institution that gives Theo belonging.

chapters.title: A House That Drowned
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Theo pulls flood records and finds contradictions: the Marlowe house's insurance claim lists contents that never appear in the salvage inventories. A retired surveyor mentions the water line was 'too tidy.' POV: Theo, with surveyor interlude. Beat: the case hooks Theo's pride — they never take one they can't close.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Theo visits Marlowe House's surviving heir, Vivian Marlowe-Ashe, Edmund's sister, who receives them with impeccable coldness and one slip: she refers to her father as 'the man in the photographs.' POV: Theo. Beat: Theo recognizes the loneliness of someone guarding a secret alone.

chapters.title: Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Rereading the confession, Theo notices its phrasing echoes the cathedral's donor plaques in the nave. Dates and amounts on the plaques, read in sequence, form a numeric key. POV: Theo. Beat: exhilaration — the thrill of pattern, the closest thing Theo has to intimacy.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Marlowe
chapters.summary: The key opens a deposit box holding photographs: Edmund's father, Sir Alistair, beside a servant named Tomas Reeve — the two men nearly identical. A 1946 wage ledger shows Reeve's pay continuing after his supposed dismissal. POV: Theo. Beat: vertigo; identity itself begins to feel negotiable.

chapters.title: What the Flood Washed In
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, 1947, from Tomas Reeve's perspective: the real Alistair Marlowe dies suddenly; the family, facing ruin and scandal, buries the servant under the name and floods the house to destroy the evidence. Beat: sympathy for the buried man; power shown corrupting everyone it touches.

chapters.title: Statute of Limitations
chapters.summary: Theo learns the confession's urgency: a legal challenge to the Marlowe inheritance expires in eleven days, after which the fraud — and the murder, if it was one — becomes untouchable. Someone has already filed it. POV: Theo. Beat: the clock starts; curiosity hardens into obligation.

chapters.title: The Dean's Quiet Hand
chapters.summary: Theo discovers the 1947 sealing order was countersigned by a dean whose private papers show a Marlowe 'donation' the same month. The church was paid to forget. POV: Theo. Beat: betrayal — the institution Theo belongs to was complicit.

chapters.title: Vivian's Version
chapters.summary: Confronted gently, Vivian tells her story: she learned the truth at nineteen and has spent fifty years protecting her father's name — and her own inheritance. She denies writing the confession. POV: Theo, with Vivian's account. Beat: doubt creeps in; Theo's certainty cracks.

chapters.title: The Confession's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Forensic comparison suggests the confession was written by someone elderly, left-handed, and familiar with the cathedral's liturgical calendar — details that fit neither Vivian nor Edmund. Theo widens the search to household staff. POV: Theo. Beat: the mystery turns inward, toward the cathedral itself.

chapters.title: The Sexton's Daughter
chapters.summary: Theo finds Edith Carrow, daughter of the 1947 sexton, now in a care home. She reveals her father helped stage the flood and kept the true ledger as insurance — and that he drowned under suspicious circumstances a year later. POV: Theo. Beat: grief for the small people crushed beneath great names.

chapters.title: Where the Ledger Sleeps
chapters.summary: Edith's clue — 'he gave it back to the church, in the place they count what's given' — leads Theo to the plaque key's second layer: amounts that map to crypt burial plots. The ledger is in the crypt. POV: Theo. Beat: dread and resolve; the locked door must be opened.

chapters.title: Breaking the Seal
chapters.summary: Theo persuades the diocesan conservator to authorize an inspection, but the night before, someone ransacks the archive and steals the confession letter. Only three people knew where it was kept. POV: Theo. Beat: violation; the invisible archivist has been seen.

chapters.title: Three Suspects, One Key
chapters.summary: Theo narrows the theft: the dean's verger, Vivian's solicitor, or Edith's grandson — each with access, each with a motive tied to the inheritance challenge. POV: Theo, rotating interviews. Beat: paranoia; every ally now a suspect.

chapters.title: The Verger Confesses to the Wrong Thing
chapters.summary: The verger admits he was paid by the solicitor to 'tidy the archive' but swears he only photographed pages, never took the letter — and shows Theo a page he did take: Edmund's death certificate, signed by a doctor who died in 1990. POV: Theo. Beat: the impossible detail — who certified a death they couldn't have witnessed?

chapters.title: Edmund Knew
chapters.summary: Reconstructing Edmund's final months, Theo finds he had commissioned his own genealogy — and received the results two weeks before his death. Edmund knew what he was. The confession letter's author feared Edmund would go public. POV: Theo. Beat: the victim becomes the catalyst; stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: Vivian's Long Silence
chapters.summary: Theo confronts Vivian with the genealogy receipt. She breaks: she didn't kill Edmund, but she wrote the confession — dictated to her, she claims, by Edmund himself the night before he died, as insurance against his own family. POV: Theo and Vivian. Beat: pity and suspicion entangled.

chapters.title: Into the Crypt
chapters.summary: The conservator's team opens the crypt. Behind the 1947 brickwork: Tomas Reeve's true remains, and in the sexton's plot niche, the Carrow ledger — names, payments, and the doctor's note confirming Alistair's death was poison. POV: Theo. Beat: awe and horror; the past is physically, bodily present.

chapters.title: The Statute Expires at Midnight
chapters.summary: The solicitor, exposed as Edmund's blackmailer and the poisoner's descendant, tries to burn the ledger; Theo and Vivian stop him, and his arrest makes the legal challenge moot — the truth enters the record hours before the deadline. POV: Theo. Beat: climax; power's corruption answered by the stubbornness of paper.

chapters.title: Names in the Record
chapters.summary: The diocese, shamed, reburied Tomas Reeve under his own name with a public service. Vivian, stripped of the tainted inheritance, donates the estate to the cathedral school. Theo testifies, visible at last. POV: Theo. Beat: cost and release; belonging rebuilt on honesty rather than silence.

chapters.title: The Case Theo Couldn't Close
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo files the final report and leaves one question deliberately open: who mailed the confession — Edmund's foresight, Vivian's conscience, or Edith's revenge? Theo shelves it unfinished, the first case they've ever let go. POV: Theo, closing reflection. Beat: peace with ambiguity; the archivist finally lets one record stay open.
